marking_memo.question:
Consider $f(x)=\ln(x-1)$ on its real domain. Show your working for the numerical estimates.

Use 4 equal trapeziums to estimate $I=\int_{2}^{10}\ln(x-1)\,dx$. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.

Hence, showing the transformation, estimate $J=\int_{2}^{10}3\ln(x^2-2x+1)\,dx$. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.

Sketch $y=\ln(x-1)$, labelling axis intersections and any vertical asymptote.

Use your sketch to decide whether the estimate in part (a) is too large (an overestimate) or too small (an underestimate). Explain how the trapezium top edges sit relative to the curve.
marking_memo.canonical_answer:
$I \approx 11.5$.

$J \approx 69.0$ using guard digits from (a).

One log branch for $x>1$, tending downwards as $x\to 1^+$, increasing with decreasing gradient; vertical asymptote $x=1$ and labelled intercept $(2,0)$; no $y$-intercept or finite horizontal asymptote.

Underestimate: the curve is concave down on the interval, so the top chords of the trapeziums lie below the curve.
marking_memo.grading_guide_answer:
Part a
$I \approx 11.5$.
WB8227-trapezium-sketch-estimate:a:B1 [1]: Positive width 2, unsimplified or in the formula.
WB8227-trapezium-sketch-estimate:a:M1 [1]: Correct trapezium weighting or actual sum of trapezium areas using a positive width.
WB8227-trapezium-sketch-estimate:a:A1 [1]: Correct 3 significant figure result 11.5, with the required valid method.
Find the width and ordinates. — Equal strips have width equal to the interval length divided by the strip count. — $\Delta x=8/4=2$; $y_{0}=\ln(1)$, $y_{1}=\ln(3)$, $y_{2}=\ln(5)$, $y_{3}=\ln(7)$, $y_{4}=\ln(9)$.
Apply the trapezium weights. — Each interior ordinate belongs to two neighbouring trapeziums. — $T=\left(y_0+2(y_{1}+y_{2}+y_{3})+y_{4}\right)\approx 11.5051453$.
Round only the reported result. — Guard digits avoid premature-rounding error. — $I \approx 11.5$ to 3 significant figures.

Part b
$J \approx 69.0$ using guard digits from (a).
WB8227-trapezium-sketch-estimate:b:B1 [1]: Factorised form $3\ln((x-1)^2)$ alone, the correct $6\ln(x-1)$, or a correctly derived 6 scale; the direct expression implies the square.
WB8227-trapezium-sketch-estimate:b:B2 [1]: Correct visible 6 times the learner own (a) estimate, with no visibly wrong log-law reasoning; exact product or any rendering correct to at least 3 significant figures.
Recognise the square. — The expanded quadratic is a perfect square. — $x^2-2x+1=(x-1)^2$.
Use the logarithm power rule. — Throughout the integration interval, $x-1>0$. — $3\ln((x-1)^2)=6\ln(x-1)$.
Scale the previous estimate. — The same bounds are used, so the factor multiplies the whole estimate. — $J\approx 6T\approx 69.0308717\approx 69.0$ (3 significant figures).

Part c
One log branch for $x>1$, tending downwards as $x\to 1^+$, increasing with decreasing gradient; vertical asymptote $x=1$ and labelled intercept $(2,0)$; no $y$-intercept or finite horizontal asymptote.
WB8227-trapezium-sketch-estimate:c:B1 [1]: Single log-shaped function graph relative to its approached boundary: right-hand branch, downwards approach without crossing/touching, rising through below/above-axis regions with decreasing gradient and no finite horizontal asymptote.
WB8227-trapezium-sketch-estimate:c:B2 [1]: Correct asymptote x=1 identified on the sketch by a labelled guide or clearly labelled approached boundary; detached text is insufficient.
WB8227-trapezium-sketch-estimate:c:B3 [1]: Correct intercept (2,0), labelled on the sketch.
Set the logarithm argument positive. — A real logarithm needs a positive argument. — $x>1$; the approached vertical boundary is $x=1$.
Locate the axis intersection. — The logarithm equals zero when its argument is one. — $x-1=1$, so the intercept is $(2,0)$; $x=0$ is outside the domain.
Draw the translated logarithm branch. — Translation preserves its increasing, concave-down shape. — The curve lies to the right of $x=1$, falls without bound near that line, and rises without a finite horizontal asymptote.

Part d
Underestimate: the curve is concave down on the interval, so the top chords of the trapeziums lie below the curve.
WB8227-trapezium-sketch-estimate:d:B1 [1]: Bias conclusion supported by the learner own sketch on (a) interval; concave-up own curve supports over, concave-down supports under. Absent sketch earns no credit; unreadable evidence is pending.
WB8227-trapezium-sketch-estimate:d:DB1 [1]: Correct top-chord/trapezium position relative to the same own curve; verbal geometric reason or correct overlay with a brief referring statement. Unambiguous concavity shorthand for the same own curve can establish the geometry; increasing alone cannot.
Compare each top chord with the curve. — The logarithm has decreasing gradient on the integration interval. — Each straight top chord lies below the concave-down curve.
Relate the areas. — The trapezium tops lie below the graph on the same positive interval. — The estimated area is smaller than the area under the curve, so it is an underestimate.

Consider $f(x)=\ln(x-1)$ on its real domain. Show your working for the numerical estimates.

$I \approx 11.5$.

$J \approx 69.0$ using guard digits from (a).

## Learning text and feedback

Use the existing guideline snapshots indexed by
`workbench/playbook/guidelines/provenance.json` (7 November 2026, file digests pinned
in the planning manifest). Those were local app snapshots, not proof of deployed
bytes. No forked shared AI instruction is added. Use British spelling, clear
English, decoded Markdown/LaTeX, separate equations and correct mathematical units.
Never put mathematical notation inside emphasis or expose provider/internal keys
as learner copy. Render all later question, help, solution, feedback and history
surfaces; a tolerant formatter does not establish authoring compliance.

Feedback recognises demonstrated work, names the first evidenced error and offers
an action/reason/result repair. It distinguishes an ambiguous upload from a wrong
answer, and the app retains the original attempt. No invented misconception is
labelled examiner-evidenced. Solutions/support and ordinary practice do not move
memory boxes; the application owns reliable completed-test progress.
